resources.string: Shows assistance controls and operates Android magnification on request.
Your screen should adapt to your eyes, not the other way around.
VueConfort helps you read more comfortably with Android magnification, custom profiles, an adapted reader and visual screening tests.
VueConfort does not replace glasses, an optician or an ophthalmologist. Some features require the Android accessibility service, which you remain free to enable or disable.
Profiles, settings and results remain locally on this device. No account, server, advertising or analytics is used.
This guide checks essential permissions and prepares your profile without blocking access to the app.

VueConfort uses the service to show the bar, control magnification, detect the active app and extract its accessible text only when you choose Read. This information stays on the device: it is neither stored nor shared.
Allow the persistent notification to see VueConfort status and use quick actions.
Allow background activity and remove VueConfort from deep sleeping apps if One UI stops the service. This recommendation is optional.
Choose the profile closest to your needs. You can change it later.
The bar appears automatically when the VueConfort accessibility service is active.
Check the bar, leave VueConfort, open another app, use + and −, then return here.
This is the actual detected status. You can run setup again from Settings.
Quick tile: Android cannot determine whether it was added
Your screen adapts to your eyes.
Optimise text presentation to reduce visual effort and improve reading comfort.
VueConfort does not replace an eye examination, suitable glasses, an optician or an ophthalmologist.
Enable the service in Android settings, check the floating bar, choose a profile, then adjust magnification with + and −.
Drag to move it. Long-press to lock it. Reduce collapses it. Recenter moves zoom back, Reset returns to 1×, Read opens the reader and Profile changes active settings.
Read only uses accessibility information exposed by the app. Games, videos, images, WebViews or protected screens may provide no text. No screenshot or global OCR is used.
A rule can use the app, time or ambient light. Manual pause temporarily prevents automatic changes.

Tests are on-screen screening estimates. Physical calibration is required. OD is right eye, OG left eye and OU both eyes. logMAR describes acuity. Repeated decline or anomalies require professional assessment.
Likely cause: inactive or interrupted service. Re-enable VueConfort in Accessibility and check Samsung battery settings.
The Android controller may be unavailable or already in use. Reset, then re-enable the service.
The current app probably exposes no accessible text. Protected content is never bypassed.
One UI may limit background use. Remove VueConfort from deep sleep and allow background activity.
Allow notifications in Settings › Apps › VueConfort › Notifications.
Check Battery › Background usage limits and Deep sleeping apps.
Open Quick Settings, choose Edit and add the VueConfort tile.
Check that the rule is active, its profile still exists and automation is not paused.

Profiles, settings, screening results, automatic rules, calibration, history and accessible text temporarily extracted at your request.
Local device storage. No account, server, advertising, analytics or network transfer added by VueConfort.
It controls magnification, shows controls, detects the active app and extracts accessible text on request. No password is stored, no screen is captured and no content is transmitted.
Non-diagnostic screening tools, not equivalent to a prescription. Results remain local and can be deleted.
You can delete history, restore profiles, clear rules or settings, disable the service and uninstall the app.

To display a magnified area, VueConfort temporarily analyses the image visible on screen using the Android accessibility service. The image is processed only on this device, in memory, then immediately discarded. It is neither saved nor transmitted. Secure screens are not captured.
Enable VueConfort in seconds. The floating bar appears as soon as the accessibility service is allowed.

VueConfort uses the accessibility service to show the floating bar, control Android magnification, detect the active app for automatic profiles, and extract accessible text only when you choose Read. This information is processed locally on this device, is not sold, and is not transmitted to a server.
